summary: Registering a Discord application and getting OAuth2 working is quick: create the app, grab the client ID and secret, and use the authorization code grant against discord.com/oauth2/authorize. There is no review to start building. Two things add friction later: some scopes require Discord's approval to use, and a bot that grows past 100 servers must pass Discord's bot verification to keep joining new servers.

oauthAvailability.note: Supports authorization code, implicit, client credentials, and bot/webhook flows. Some scopes need Discord approval.

difficulty.reason: A single registration and standard OAuth2; review only appears for restricted scopes or large bots.

approvalWait.note: No review to start; bot verification applies only past 100 servers.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: Registering the app and wiring the OAuth2 flow; nothing to wait on for a standard integration.

review.requiredWhen: Not required for standard OAuth2. Bot verification becomes mandatory to join new servers once a bot is in 100+ servers; some scopes require Discord approval.

prerequisites.detail: Used to create the application in the Developer Portal.

prerequisites.item: An application registered in the Developer Portal

steps.title: Register an application and copy credentials
steps.detail: Create a new application in the Discord Developer Portal and copy the client_id and client_secret. Keep the secret handy for the token exchange.

steps.title: Configure OAuth2 and redirect URLs
steps.detail: Under OAuth2, add your redirect URL(s) and select the scopes your integration needs (for example identify, email, guilds).

steps.title: Implement the authorization code grant
steps.detail: Send users to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize with your client_id, scopes, and redirect_uri, then exchange the returned code at https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token for an access token.
steps.gotcha: Requesting an approval-gated scope without Discord's approval can cause errors or undocumented behavior in the flow.

steps.title: Plan for bot verification if you ship a bot
steps.detail: If your app includes a bot, note that once it is in 100+ servers it must complete Discord's bot verification to continue joining new servers.

notes: Redirect URLs are registered under the application's OAuth2 settings.
The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match a registered URL.

recommended.purpose: Read the user's account without email.
List basic information about the user's guilds.
Add a bot to a selected guild.

sensitive.consequence: Updates command permissions in a guild; use carefully.
Reads a user's friends, pending requests, and blocked users; part of the Social SDK and requires submitting for access.
Only available to approved partners; reads information about the user's DMs.

notes: Several scopes (e.g. applications.builds.upload, rpc, dm_channels.read) are only available to approved partners.
Requesting approval-gated scopes without approval can break the OAuth2 flow.

blockers.title: Bot cannot join new servers
blockers.symptom: A popular bot stops being able to join additional servers.
blockers.cause: The bot reached 100+ servers without completing Discord's bot verification.
blockers.resolution: Complete bot verification to continue scaling past the 100-server threshold.

blockers.title: Scope request errors
blockers.symptom: The OAuth2 flow errors or behaves unexpectedly for certain scopes.
blockers.cause: An approval-gated or partner-only scope was requested without Discord's approval.
blockers.resolution: Remove the scope or submit for access/approval before requesting it.

humanMust: Register the application and hold the client secret
Submit for bot verification or partner-only scope access when required
handoffPoints: Agent builds the OAuth2 flow; a human handles verification and partner-scope approvals.
